blocks.text: Jesus’ reference to “the sign of Jonah” has prompted debate. Matthew connects Jonah’s three days and nights with the Son of Man and also recalls Nineveh’s response, while Luke presents Jonah as a sign and emphasizes Nineveh’s response to his proclamation. These differing emphases shape how readers understand the brief reference in Matthew 16.

Peter’s confession is followed by sayings about Peter, the rock, the church, the keys of the kingdom, and binding and loosing. Matthew uniquely brings these elements together in this scene, and their meaning has generated major disputes about the church and Peter’s role.
